description: Add a project-scoped InboxSubscription preference (four notification-kind toggles, all-enabled default) that gates the inbox projection, expose it through a project-scoped read/update HTTP API, and surface it in a dedicated Web inbox settings tab with product-facing labels.

tasks.title: InboxSubscription preference model, EF table, scoped store, and migration
tasks.description: Add the server-side InboxSubscription persistence foundation: an InboxSubscriptions table (PK ProjectId, 1:1 with Projects) with four bool columns (WorkflowFailedEnabled, ApprovalRequestedEnabled, IssueStartedEnabled, IssueCompletedEnabled) plus UpdatedAt; an InboxSubscriptionRow entity; and a scoped InboxSubscriptionStore : IScopedService mirroring ProjectWorkflowProfileManager's load-by-projectId / null-synthesizes-default / mutate / SaveChanges shape. Reads MUST synthesize all-four-enabled when no row exists (no eager row creation on project create or first read). Add the EF migration mirroring 20260629003151_AddInboxItemsTable and regenerate MohistDbContextModelSnapshot. The store is auto-registered by AddMohistConventionalServices via the IScopedService marker, so no manual DI wiring.
acceptanceCriteria: Reading a project with no stored row returns all four kinds enabled (synthesized default), keyed by NotificationKind.
An update persists a new row; a subsequent read returns the persisted toggle states.
A second update on the same project mutates the existing row in place (no duplicate rows).
InboxSubscriptions table is created by a new EF migration with PK ProjectId, FK to Projects(Id), four non-nullable bool columns, and UpdatedAt; MohistDbContextModelSnapshot is regenerated.
MohistStore registration is picked up via IScopedService (no manual AddSingleton/AddScoped wiring).
`npm test` (dotnet build with TreatWarningsAsErrors) passes and the new store unit tests cover default-all-enabled, persist, re-read, and in-place mutation.
tasks.output: New InboxSubscriptionRow.cs, InboxSubscriptionStore.cs, InboxSubscription view/model, updated MohistDbContext (DbSet + OnModelCreating config), new migration <timestamp>_AddInboxSubscriptionsTable.cs (+.Designer.cs), regenerated MohistDbContextModelSnapshot.cs, and store unit tests.
tasks.notes: Follow D1 (EF, not Orleans grain) and D2/D3 (one row per project, four bool columns, no eager creation, missing == all-enabled). This is the shared foundation consumed by both the projection gate (T-002) and the HTTP API (T-003).

tasks.title: Subscription-gated inbox projection
tasks.description: Modify InboxProjectionHandler.ProjectAsync to gate inserts by the owning project's subscription: after `resolved` and `kind` are known (~InboxProjectionHandler.cs:140) and before inboxStore.InsertAsync (~:149), resolve InboxSubscriptionStore from the already-open DI scope (InboxProjectionHandler.cs:114) and read the project's subscription; if the resolved kind's toggle is disabled, return early with no insert and no realtime hint publish. A project with no stored subscription is treated as all-enabled via the store's synthesized default. No in-process cache; idempotency is preserved because a skipped event is never inserted.
acceptanceCriteria: Projection creates the inbox item when the event's kind is enabled for the owning project (all four kinds verified across the four authoritative events).
Projection performs NO insert and publishes NO InboxItemPersisted hint when the event's kind is disabled for the owning project.
Projection creates the item for a project with no stored subscription (treats as all-enabled), preserving MVP behavior.
Re-enabling a previously-disabled kind allows the next observed event of that kind to insert; no backfill of events skipped while disabled.
Disabling a kind leaves existing inbox items of that kind untouched (not deleted, rewritten, or marked read).
Replaying a disabled-kind event remains a no-op (idempotency intact).
Projection unit tests cover enabled, disabled, missing-default, and re-enabled behavior, and assert existing items are unchanged.
tasks.output: Modified InboxProjectionHandler.cs and updated/added projection tests.
tasks.notes: Follow D4: one extra store read in the existing scope before insert; no cache. The early-return must skip both InsertAsync and the IEventPublisher hint publish. Realtime/SignalR connection subscriptions are NOT affected (spec: separate from durable subscription).

tasks.title: Project-scoped subscription read and update HTTP API
tasks.description: Extend the existing InboxRoutes group (same /api/projects/{projectRef}/inbox prefix, same ProjectResolutionEndpointFilter, same project isolation) with two endpoints: GET /subscription returns the four toggles keyed by NotificationKind (all-enabled when no stored row); PUT /subscription accepts a whole-object replace of the four toggles keyed by NotificationKind and persists via InboxSubscriptionStore. PUT SHALL reject any key failing NotificationKinds.IsDefined (or any missing/extra key) with ApiResults.BadRequest. Define request/response DTOs inline in the route file with a FromState/ToState mapper, mirroring InboxItemDto.FromView (InboxRoutes.cs:83-108). Use PUT whole-object replace semantics, not PATCH-merge.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /subscription on a project with no stored preferences returns all four kinds as enabled, keyed by NotificationKind (workflow_failed, approval_requested, issue_started, issue_completed).
PUT /subscription persists the four toggles; a subsequent GET returns the updated state.
PUT with an unknown/extra key (not one of the four NotificationKind values) is rejected with a 400 BadRequest and persists nothing.
A subscription operation scoped to project A never reads or mutates project B's subscription (ProjectResolutionEndpointFilter scoping).
DTOs are defined inline in InboxRoutes.cs with FromState/ToState mappers; no raw CloudEvent type strings appear in the API contract.
API tests cover read (stored + default), update + re-read, unknown-key rejection, and project isolation.
tasks.output: Modified InboxRoutes.cs (new GET/PUT /subscription endpoints + inline DTOs) and API tests.
tasks.notes: Follow D5 (PUT whole-object replace, inline DTOs). Independent of T-002 (projection) — both consume the T-001 store in parallel.

tasks.title: Web inbox subscription settings surface
tasks.description: Add the Web data layer and settings UI for inbox subscriptions. Under packages/web/src/entities/inbox/api/: add an API client function for GET/PUT /inbox/subscription, a subscriptionQueryKey = (projectId) => ['inbox-subscription', projectId], useInboxSubscription() query, and useUpdateInboxSubscription() mutation that invalidates only ['inbox-subscription', projectId] on success (NOT ['inbox', projectId], since toggling affects only future projection). Add a new 'inbox' section to VALID_SECTIONS/SECTION_META in SettingsPage.tsx and a new InboxSubscriptionSection.tsx rendering four @base-ui/react/switch toggles inline, each wrapped with a Label and showing product-facing labels reused from KIND_DESCRIPTORS (InboxPage.tsx). PreferencesSection.tsx MUST remain untouched (its non-goal guard fails the build if 'notification' appears there).
acceptanceCriteria: The new settings tab renders exactly one toggle per notification kind, each with a product-facing label ('Workflow failed', 'Approval requested', 'Issue started', 'Issue completed') and NO raw event or CloudEvent type names.
Toggles reflect the currently persisted subscription state; a project with no stored preferences shows all four toggles enabled.
Changing a toggle persists through the inbox subscription HTTP API (PUT) and the query refetches/invalidates correctly; the inbox list query is NOT invalidated.
PreferencesSection.tsx is unchanged and PreferencesSection.test.tsx non-goal guard still passes.
Each toggle has an accessible name (Label wrapping) satisfying the aria-toggle-field-name a11y rule.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass, including new hook and section tests.
tasks.output: New/updated files under packages/web/src/entities/inbox/api/ (client + hooks + query key), new InboxSubscriptionSection.tsx, modified SettingsPage.tsx (new 'inbox' section), and corresponding tests.
tasks.notes: Follow D6: dedicated new 'inbox' tab (not PreferencesSection); reuse KIND_DESCRIPTORS from InboxPage.tsx for labels; use @base-ui/react/switch inline (no new shared component yet). Open question from design: do NOT invalidate the unread-count/inbox list query when toggling.
